_comment: Ceiling on unresolved cross-references in data/, enforced by tools/validate.py.
BASELINE: 110 when this check was added -- the measured count, so CI went
green on the committed debt and red on any NEW dangling reference.
It is already ratcheting down as the dangling references get fixed; this
file is kept at the CURRENT count so a single new one fails CI. When a
change REDUCES the count, lower this in that same change -- validate.py
prints the exact figure to copy. Never RAISE it to make CI pass.

2026-10-04: lowered 54 -> 43. The A100 disambiguation pass resolved 11 of the 29 nvidia-a100-sxm references on evidence quoted from the papers themselves, and the benchmark/quantization passes repaid more. Lowered in the same change that reduced the count, which is the rule; raising it to go green is never correct.

2026-10-05: lowered 43 -> 30. The paper-duplicate consolidation removed 15 retired slugs (each verified to have zero inbound references) and repaid one more that pointed at a nonexistent hardware id. Lowered in the same change that reduced the count, which is the rule.

2026-10-10: lowered 30 -> 13. The nvidia-a100-sxm dangling references were repaid by CREATING the missing target rather than editing the citations: a new canonical accelerator record data/accelerators/nvidia-a100-sxm.json (A100 SXM, capacity unstated) is now the citation target for the 17 paper records that cite bare "A100" without stating a memory capacity. The 17 were never wrong -- the record they named simply did not exist -- so all 17 resolved with zero paper edits. The remaining 13 are deliberately budgeted and NOT fixable by adding records: gfx950 (4), gfx942 (3) and gfx1151 (1) are AMD architecture TARGETS (there is no part record to point at); mlx-quantized-4bit (3) and 2bit (1) are quantization FORMAT names, not ids; amd-ryzen-strix-point (1) is a CPU point on a flops record. Lowered in the same change that reduced the count, which is the rule.
